opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, write is the standard maximum; Payroll admin requires the Payroll Specialist role, so write is the appropriate level.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E007 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the maximum, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: HR (authoritative for employment type) confirms E007 Kenneth Burch is a full-time Analyst, which permits up to write access. Payroll admin requires the Payroll Specialist role, and Burch is an Analyst, so admin is not allowed and the maximum is write. The requested level (write) is at the maximum, so write is granted. Note: Security's note claims contractor status, but HR's verified record shows full-time; even considering the conflict, the requested write is appropriate under the full-time policy.

- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write
- Security agent: employment type contractor, security training basic, role Analyst, recommendation read

There's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Kenneth is an Analyst, so not owner.

If full_time: max is write (Analyst doesn't own Payroll). Requested write → grant write.
If contractor: max is read (basic training). Requested write is above max → grant read.

However, note the security agent's comment: "Security DB shows E007 is a contractor with basic security training." Security DB is likely authoritative for security training and possibly employment type? HR DB is likely authoritative for employment type.
